Levites
lē´vīts
n. pl. (the tribe of Levi set apart for sanctuary service; Hebrew Lewiyyim)
From Levi, third son of Jacob and Leah. The tribe that had been scattered in Jacob's prophecy was scattered indeed — but into the service of God.

Biblical Definition

The Levites are the tribe of Levi, taken by God out of Israel and given to Aaron for the work of the tabernacle. Their claim rests on a substitution: the LORD had sanctified every firstborn in Israel to Himself in the night of the passover, and He then took the Levites “instead of all the firstborn” (Num 3:12), so that the whole tribe stands in the room of a nation's eldest sons. They bore the ark, they camped around the tabernacle as a living fence between the holy things and the congregation, they taught the law, and they blessed in the LORD's name. They received no territorial inheritance; the tenth in Israel was given them instead, and the LORD Himself was called their portion. Jacob had prophesied that Levi would be divided in Jacob and scattered in Israel — a word spoken in rebuke for the violence at Shechem, yet fulfilled in mercy, for the scattering became forty-eight cities of instruction sown through every tribe. The order is typical throughout: a people substituted, a service assigned, an inheritance that is God Himself.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines Levite as one of the tribe of Levi, appointed to the lower offices of the sanctuary.

expand to see more

LEVITE, n. One of the tribe or family of Levi; a descendant of Levi.

2. One of that tribe employed in the lower services of the temple, as distinguished from the priests.

LEVITICAL, a. Belonging to the Levites, or to the tribe of Levi.

LEVITICUS, n. The third book of Moses, containing the laws of the priesthood and sacrifices.

The Levites had no inheritance of land, but received the tithes of the other tribes.

Key Scripture

Num 3:12 — "And I, behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix among the children of Israel: therefore the Levites shall be mine;"

Num 8:14 — "Thus shalt thou separate the Levites from among the children of Israel: and the Levites shall be mine."

Deu 10:8 — "At that time the LORD separated the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to minister unto him, and to bless in his name, unto this day."

Num 18:21 — "And, behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance, for their service which they serve, even the service of the tabernacle of the congregation."

Modern Corruption

Set-apart service is read as clerical privilege, when Scripture presents it as substitution, labour, and the surrender of an inheritance.

expand to see more

The Levite is often imagined as a man of leisure kept by other men's tithes — a caste enjoying religion at the nation's expense. The text says the reverse. The Levites carried the tabernacle on their shoulders, guarded its vessels on pain of death, and were forbidden the one thing every other Israelite received: land. The tenth was not a salary but the substitute for an inheritance, and it came with the charge that they themselves tithe of the tithe. Their honour and their loss were the same fact.

The recovery is to see the whole tribe as a standing type. They were taken instead of the firstborn, which is the logic of substitution written into the census; they had no portion, which is the logic of the minister who lives by the altar; and they blessed in the LORD's name, which is the logic of a mediated word. All of it points forward to the one Levite's better than Levi, the Priest after the order of Melchisedec, and to a people made kings and priests who likewise hold their true inheritance in God and not in ground.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Lewi (H3878), Levi, ‘joined’; Lewiyyi (H3881), a Levite; Greek Leuites (G3019).

expand to see more

Hebrew Lewi (H3878) — Levi, from lawah, to join; Genesis 29:34.

Hebrew Lewiyyi (H3881) — a Levite; Numbers 3:12, Deuteronomy 10:8.

Hebrew maaser (H4643) — a tenth, the tithe given the Levites; Numbers 18:21.

Greek Leuites (G3019) — a Levite; Luke 10:32, John 1:19, Acts 4:36.

Jacob's word that Levi would be scattered (Genesis 49:7) was fulfilled in forty-eight Levitical cities.

Usage

"“The Levites shall be mine” — a tribe taken in the room of the firstborn."

"“To bear the ark… to stand… to bless” — the threefold Levitical charge."

"“I have given the children of Levi all the tenth” — the tithe instead of a territory."
